how: The surviving title calls members to help build a Catalan flag.
A deleted call author and several reported attempts prevent identifying the original starter or attributing later participation to that person's call.
Participants coordinate bars and blue letters and propose putting their name on the flag.
A participant reports a continually disappearing letter while the author reports completed line changes.
A shared pattern directs placers to preserve the letters and provides a target the script author says is being followed.
Members share, explain, modify, and check an automatic flag-painting script that still places one pixel every five minutes.
Sharing machine instructions includes repeating them across languages and accepting a correction to the English wording.
A script matching the current pattern cannot align all placements unless users update their distributed versions.
Posting a pattern does not settle placement when users may still run versions that erase its letters.
A participant describes maintaining the fragmented flag against aggressors while critics contest whether the activity counts as maintenance.
The script author explicitly presents automation as answering other scripts covering the flag.
The author's stated motive establishes a response to machine opposition without independently demonstrating exhausted manual placement capacity.
Participants diagnose disappearing letters through possibly outdated scripts and an admission of their own automatic mistake.
A flag helper rejects destroying other art merely to enlarge the flag, while neighbours ask that existing logos survive.
Participants explicitly choose to respect the neighbouring flag and report modifying their script to spare another logo.
A participant reports writing to the neighbouring room to stop downward expansion and clear up mistaken blame.
One member carries the room's border request and denial of responsibility into the neighbouring room and reports awaiting its response.
An explicit script-update reply turns the discussion of respecting a neighbouring flag and displaced bars into a change to automated placement.
Internal agreement to spare a neighbour precedes any visible bilateral settlement, so restraint here does not require an already settled border.
Naming the flag is proposed to prevent confusion about who is attacking the neighbour, extending design work into attribution repair.
A visitor conditionally offers upkeep in exchange for preserving a small design on the flag.
An individual offers help after pausing work on a hammer and sickle and receives the flag builder's thanks.
A conditional offer couples space and upkeep in one turn without demonstrating that settled border talk produced delivered help.
The flag's asserted host rule prohibits guest drawings, while a separate title permits one named exception without proving recognized authority.
A visitor seeks protection for a small design already being made inside the flag rather than merely negotiating an adjacent border.
A moderator questions the flag's point and receives a defence based on enjoyment and visibility, fitting worth-questioning without showing posting restrictions.
A call preceding questions about the flag's worth does not establish that a flood of canvas posts prompted those questions.
The builder credits an active helper with thanks during ongoing coordination, without announcing that the work is finished.
Thanks for present help do not establish the proposed completion-to-celebration mechanism while design and access problems remain in the thread.
A brief thanks answers a correction of the script instructions without asking anything back.
An invasion dispute continues through a sarcastic challenge to maintenance and a dismissal of the critic as ignorant.
Participants accuse flag builders of attack and destroying a logo, supporting reported encroachment rather than an independently observed coordinated raid.

statement: reporting an unexplained blank canvas during ongoing work
how: The isolated blank-canvas report preserves an unexplained access problem without establishing a timer workaround, remedy, or resulting interruption of placements.
A blanket rule, an exception, and open debate do not express a dispute over whether one member can bind other placers.
Deleted announcement bodies and one-sided outreach cannot test whether an inter-room agreement generated a dispute about authority to commit placers.
Pre-closure thanks and a blank-canvas report cannot test disputes over which post-closure version of the event should be preserved.
A possible alliance is offered without a visible acceptance or shared defence that would establish a coalition.
The smaller-flag suggestion argues that modest visibility is enough rather than documenting a judgement of insufficient hands.
Debating a smaller flag does not establish erasure followed by a decision to relocate.
Open invitations to contribute and debate cannot establish the absence of decided order, and one room cannot test the cross-room frequency claim.
Liking a national flag and contrasting its size with Germany do not establish politics or collective identity beyond the flag.
Accusing invaders and invoking Germany as a size comparison do not identify a quarrel carried in from before the canvas.
The comparison with Germany does not name a prior tie as the reason for calling or carrying out an attack.
A laugh marker while explaining why they draw the flag does not establish an April Fools parody or fake canvas call.
The title-only event trace cannot identify retrospective recording, and the closing thanks names no saved record.
Thanks during the active effort and an unspecified event title supply no visible proposal for carrying the work onward.
Acknowledging a helper without identifiable later preservation cannot test a transition from crediting work to recording it.
An unspecified event title and pre-closure thanks cannot test whether recording the work led to a continuing project.
Bare thanks answer an apology, wording repair, and offered help rather than demonstrating that the original build call elicited bare joining replies.
A build call and later accusations of encroachment do not preserve an explicit attack call attributable to that recruitment.
A reasoned objection to destroying art follows a logo complaint through a deleted turn, leaving no visible attack call whose refusal it establishes.
A volunteered offer and thanks do not show that a shortage of defenders caused the room to seek outside help.
